pages.summary: Users, units, and permission boundaries in the Hull form — opaque tokens, presence split by form, the unit tree, levels and credits, worker cards, and data isolation.

pages.title: Interlink
pages.summary: Device management, workspace access, and thread control after a local workbench signs in to the cloud.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: One core and engine shared by the four forms, the fixed path a message takes inside a session, storage choices, bounded views, external interfaces, and runtime defaults.

pages.title: Agent Loop
pages.summary: The model-round granularity of the main loop, round and tool-call budgets, circuit-breaking and timeout guardrails, and the frozen system prompt of a thread.

pages.title: Tools
pages.summary: How the four layers — tools, skills, capabilities, and user tools — are told apart, canonical names and aliases, dispatch order for dynamic registration, default sets and visibility gates, and the two result-trimming tracks.

pages.title: Tool System
pages.summary: The path a tool call takes from parsing, orchestration, and dispatch to persistence, reasons a tool is invisible, naming and registration, parallelism, timeouts, budgets, clipping, and MCP integration.

pages.title: Realtime
pages.summary: WebSocket endpoints and event categories, cursor-based catch-up after a disconnect, backpressure and slow-client uncoupling on a bounded projection, and interlink as a separate realtime path.

pages.title: Stability
pages.summary: Four kinds of hard constraint — bounded queues, limits and budgets, session locks with a single writer, and circuit-breaker thresholds — plus a uniform error structure and a symptom-to-action table.

pages.title: Observability
pages.summary: What logs, runtime metrics and alerts, monitoring and thread traces, and performance testing each cover, and the troubleshooting flow that starts from the structured error.

pages.title: Workspaces and the Working Directory
pages.summary: One workspace per user isolation policy, location and the three firm rules on the Pupa and the Hull, file operations, usage statistics, and the local boundary.

pages.title: Sessions and Rounds
pages.summary: The four-layer numbering of threads, user rounds, model rounds, and entries, plus counting conventions, idempotency and queueing, timeline entries, and interface reading.

pages.title: Streaming Execution
pages.summary: Persist-then-notify channel ordering, the WebSocket channel list, four event classes, cursor-based resumption, and the default bounds.

pages.title: Runtime and Online Status
pages.summary: The six runtime states of a session, interface badges and indicators, how to judge a stuck session, and the sequence for handling inconsistent state.

pages.title: Prompts and Skills
pages.summary: Composition and freezing of the system prompt, the three layers of skills, switching template packs and where changes apply, and the division of responsibility.

pages.title: Long-term Memory
pages.summary: Injection and freezing rules for structured memory fragments, what memory can hold, initialization injection versus runtime recall, and how it differs from the knowledge base.

pages.title: Quota and Token Usage
pages.summary: How the 1-credit-per-model-request and 1000-per-day grant are issued and deducted, and what the token metrics observe.

pages.title: Goal Mode
pages.summary: Fields of a session-level persistent goal, the four phases and the continuation gate, the in-process arming flag, model-side operations, and the available entry points.

pages.title: Companion System
pages.summary: ZIP package and sprite-sheet specification, per-form presentation, scale and position ranges, and user versus administrator permissions.

pages.title: Boundary Handling
pages.summary: Graduated compression on context overflow, reconnect and event replay after a disconnect, tool failure handling by type, and queueing with priority.

pages.title: Session Status Guide
pages.summary: When the waiting, thinking, running tools, approval, failed, cancelled, stuck and connection statuses appear, what they mean, and how to handle them.

pages.title: Prompts and Personalization
pages.summary: The built-in packs `default-zh` and `default-en`, the segments a pack is made of, switching and effect rules, and how to create a custom pack.

pages.title: System Settings Reference
pages.summary: The six settings categories, configuration layers and effect timing, and a configuration comparison across two deployment forms.

pages.title: Workspace Routing and File Management
pages.summary: Uniqueness and isolation of the cloud directory, how `/wunder/workspace*` is resolved, path conventions, usage statistics, and file management.

pages.title: Bridge Panel Guide
pages.summary: What each panel in the four groups manages, plus the throughput-test, simulated-model, and random-simulator conventions.

pages.title: WeChat iLink Channel
pages.summary: How `weixin` compares with the legacy WeChat channels, QR-code sign-in, required and optional configuration, media and inbound troubleshooting, and migration steps.

pages.title: Chat WebSocket
pages.summary: The handshake flow, client message types, server returns, and reconnect behavior of `/wunder/chat/ws`.

pages.title: MCP Endpoint
pages.summary: The address and transport of the MCP service wunder exposes, the built-in `excute` and `doc2md` tools, and how to configure an external MCP service.
